 Order

This writ petition has been filed challenging the award passed in Award No.1/2020 dated 05.11.2020 passed by the third respondent and for a consequential direction to the third respondent to pass the award with respect to the subject property belonging to the petitioners.
2. The award passed by the third respondent has been primarily challenged on two grounds.

The first ground is that the award was passed in the name of a dead person even though the third respondent was informed on more than one occasion that the original owner of the property namely,
Radhabai died on 31.07.2014 and therefore, the award must be held to be null and void.
The second ground that has been raised is that the lands were acquired under the Tamil Nadu Acquisition of Land https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 17/04/2025 04:41:26 pm ) Writ Petition No.10753 of 2023 for Industrial Purposes Act, 1997 and this Act was in force till the same was held to be invalid by the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court by order dated 03.07.2019.
The Act was once again revived by the Tamil Nadu Amendment Act 38/2019.

Thereby, the benefits of the Central Act 30/2013 has to be considered for determination of compensation on the date of notification under Section 11 of the Act as provided under Section 26 of the Act 30/2013.
Since the same has not been complied with, the award passed by the third respondent has to be held to be null and void.
3. A counter affidavit has been filed by the respondents 2 and 3 and they have justified the award passed by the third respondent.
4. This Court has carefully considered the submissions made on either side and materials placed before this Court.
5. In the case on hand, the original owner of the property namely, Radhabai was the owner of the property and she died on 31.07.2014.

In spite of the fact that the same was brought to the notice of t h e t h i r d r e s p o n d e n t , t h e t h i r d r e s p o n d e n t p r o c e e d e d t o p a s s t h e a w a r d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 17/04/2025 04:41:26 pm ) Writ Petition No.10753 of 2023 in the name of dead person.
On that ground alone, the award has to be held to be null and void.
The award was passed on 05.11.2020 by the third respondent when 1997 Act was in force.
Under Sub-Section 11 of Section 7, determination of compensation must be made within a period of six months from the date of reference to the Collector.
In the case on hand, the award has not been passed within the time prescribed.

That apart, the Act was held to be invalid by the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court on 03.07.2019 and the Act was thereafter revived by the Tamil Nadu Amendment Act 38/2019, which provided for the benefits of the Central Act 30/2013.
This was not even taken into consideration by the third respondent and on this ground also, the award has to be held to be null and void.
